problem: Existing VLN methods use only RGB features and neglect 3D semantic information from depth. The one prior RGB-D attempt (DASA) gave only marginal gains, since a 3D semantic encoder is hard to learn from the limited annotated VLN data, let alone jointly with the navigation model.
motivation: RGB inputs carry many semantic-irrelevant texture details, which cause overfitting and weak 3D perception. Depth-derived 3D semantic reconstruction offers higher-level structure, but a large 3D encoder needs a self-supervised pretraining route to be usable in VLN.
key_idea: Pretrain a sparse-convolution 3D semantic encoder with a self-supervised region-query task (does class c exist in 3D box?), then use its features in an LSTM navigation agent, and distill them into an RGB branch for fusion.
insight: 3D semantic features alone (66.8% SR val-unseen) beat RGB features trained the same way (58.1%), so the gain comes from the representation and not the navigation model. Naively fusing from-scratch RGB with 3D features hurts (65.7%). Distilling the RGB branch to mimic the 3D branch (RGB*) lifts RGB alone to 63.3% and fusion to 67.7%, so the two modalities are complementary once RGB is regularized.
method: 3D semantic reconstruction: Swin Transformer (ADE20k, 150 classes) segments panoramic RGB views; segmentations are projected with depth into a voxel grid (0.125 m XY, 0.25 m Z, ±8 m/±4 m) of size 150x128x128x32, stored sparsely.
Sparse conv encoder: encodes the sparse voxels to a 2048x4x4 feature F_sem.

Region query pretext task: query (x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2,class c) is encoded by an MLP into q; multi-head attention over F_sem answers True/False. Positive/negative samples are balanced per class, with noise and affine augmentation; accuracy 96.5% train / 95.4% val.

Navigation model: EnvDrop-style LSTM agent with BERT language features; cross-modal attention over language and 3D features with GELU MLP residual fusion; bilinear action scoring over viewpoint angle encodings; IL + A2C RL losses.

RGB fusion with cross-modal distillation: the ResNet-152 (Places365) RGB branch is first trained to mimic the 3D branch output (RGB*), then jointly fine-tuned with it, averaging the attention outputs.
Three-stage training: Speaker-Follower augmented data (~1M pairs from PREVALENT), then R2R train set, then joint 3D+RGB* fine-tuning.

setting.backbone: Sparse conv 3D semantic encoder (self-supervised) + Swin segmentor (ADE20k, pretrained) + BERT (last layer fine-tuned) + LSTM navigator; ResNet-152 RGB branch
setting.training_data: Region-query pretraining on 3D semantic reconstructions (unlabelled by navigation); navigation trained on R2R train plus ~1M Speaker-Follower augmented pairs from PREVALENT

results: On the R2R test-unseen server, the method reaches 66% SR / 60 SPL and 68% SR on val-unseen with only an LSTM navigator. This beats the RGB-D DASA (54% test SR) by more than 10 points and is comparable to or better than the transformer methods VLN-BERT (63%) and HAMT (65% SR test, 66% val-unseen). Replacing 3D semantic features with RGB drops val-unseen SR from 66.8 to 58.1.
limitations: Requires depth observations and a pretrained segmentor. The 150-class ADE20k semantics limit the vocabulary, and depth prediction is left to future work.
Evaluated only on R2R in the discrete simulator, with a multi-stage training pipeline and heavy 3D voxel memory cost.
Test SPL (60) equals HAMT's, and val-seen/unseen gains use longer action limits (30 steps).
